transcript:
Meeting Header: 2027-11-17 10:00 PST | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Ava Martinez, Jonah Clark (Redwood); Priya Desai, Mark Liu, Sana Patel, Luis Gomez (NexaHealth)

00:00 - Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to about 45 minutes then open for any deeper items, uh Jonah and I will run through onboarding and env readiness.
00:18 - Priya Desai: Thanks Ava, yeah we wanted to check status and make sure the infra pieces are unblocked.
00:30 - Jonah Clark: Quick agenda: access, network, security, initial perf notes, then actions. Does that work?
00:42 - Mark Liu: Works for me, we've been waiting on VPC peering details and SSH bastion instructions.
00:55 - Ava Martinez: Great, Mark earlier this week we posted the runbook link in email — link is https://drive.redwood/poc-runbook (note: placeholder). Did you get that?
01:08 - Mark Liu: I saw it but didn't have a chance to go through fully, we're blocked on approval for the peering CIDR from our infra team.
01:22 - Priya Desai: Also curious about dedicated vs hosted for the pilot, cost tradeoffs — we don't want surprises.
01:34 - Jonah Clark: Sure, for a short pilot hosted is easiest, but for consistent latency and to test production patterns dedicated or private deployment gives more deterministic results. We can model cost — Ava will follow up with pricing.
01:50 - Sana Patel: On security, we need SOC2 attestation and KMS/HSM integration info. We have strict PII rules so encryption at rest with our key is required.
02:05 - Ava Martinez: We have a SOC2 report and KMS integration pattern — I'll share the docs after the call. We support customer-managed KMS via the Private deployment; for Hosted we can discuss a bring-your-own-key approach.
02:22 - Luis Gomez: Quick perf q: when you ran the demo last week, latency seemed fine for small prompts but we saw degradation at 2k token sequences. Any known tuning?
02:36 - Jonah Clark: Yep, long context tuning is a known area — we saw throughput drop due to KV cache warms and the model's attention pattern. For the POC we recommend limiting the max length for the scoring path and enable prefix caching; we also suggested model quantization for cost.
02:56 - Speaker 1: (unintelligible) yeah, and the batching policy needs to be tuned for their traffic shape.
03:10 - Mark Liu: Can you explain prefix caching?
03:22 - Jonah Clark: Prefix or KV cache means repeated system prompts or initial conversation prefixes are cached on the server to avoid recomputing. That reduces per-token cost and latency if the workload is chatty.
03:38 - Priya Desai: That would help our chat flows. Question: do you need admin-level access to set the cache?
03:48 - Ava Martinez: No admin on their cluster; we configure via the Redwood Console or via config files if Private. For your env Mark, we just need the peering and an SSH key to access the bastion for setup.
04:05 - Mark Liu: Ok, I can add the CIDR to the ticket and share the key. Our security team wants to review SSH bastion logs retention — do you keep audit logs?
04:18 - Jonah Clark: Yes, audit logs are available and we can push logs to your SIEM or S3; retention policy is configurable but for the POC we keep 90 days by default.
04:32 - Sana Patel: Sounds good, but we need proof of encryption in transit and at rest. Also can you confirm RBAC roles for operator vs app-level users?
04:44 - Ava Martinez: We'll send the RBAC matrix in the security bundle. For Hosted you'll get RBAC via tenant roles; Private supports your SSO SAML mapping.
04:58 - Priya Desai: Any blockers on the Redwood side to connect to our staging VPC?
05:10 - Jonah Clark: Once we have the peering CIDR and firewall openings for the bastion IP (we'll provide), setup is usually 1-2 business days. The main blocker we've seen is corporate firewalls that block ephemeral ports for the initial handshake.
05:28 - Mark Liu: We had that issue last time with another vendor, yep. I'll coordinate.
05:40 - Ava Martinez: Great. On perf benchmarks — Jonah ran a run yesterday, results are preliminary, I think Jonah you wanted to summarize?
05:52 - Jonah Clark: Yeah, ran a 1k sample with the sample convo flow (sheet: shared/benchmarks.xlsx). Median latency ~220ms for short prompts on our ded pool, tail (95th) around 520ms when sequences hit 1.5k tokens. We saw better results enabling continuous batching but it increases token cost marginally.
06:18 - Luis Gomez: 520ms at 1.5k tokens sounds ok but the tail is concerning. Any immediate tuning steps?
06:28 - Jonah Clark: A few: reduce max tokens in the scoring path, enable prefix/KV caching, set batching timeout lower for low-latency routes, and consider a quantized model variant for fast inference. We can provide config diffs.
06:45 - Priya Desai: Quantization — does that impact quality? We care about hallucinations and accuracy.
06:55 - Jonah Clark: Minor delta in some cases; we recommend running a small quality test suite (we can run evals tied to your prompt set) to measure. For many retrieval-augmented tasks, quality holds up.
07:12 - Speaker 2: (crosstalk) uh yeah there's tradeoffs...
07:20 - Ava Martinez: We'll help run the quality vs cost matrix. Jonah will upload the perf results and we will attach quality evals.
07:30 - Mark Liu: On the networking side, do you support VPC peering in AWS only or GCP as well?
07:40 - Jonah Clark: We support both; peering works slightly differently but the runbook has steps for AWS/GCP/Azure. We'll tailor to your cloud.
07:54 - Sana Patel: On compliance, you mentioned sending the SOC2 report — do you have an SOC2 on the Hosted environment or only for Dedicated?
08:05 - Ava Martinez: We have SOC2 Type II for the platform; the certificate covers our hosted service. For Private deployments we provide control documents to map controls.
08:18 - Priya Desai: Good. Also, our procurement asked about contract length and SLAs for the pilot — minimums?
08:28 - Ava Martinez: For pilots we usually do a 30-60 day eval with standard T&Cs; if you'd like SLA-backed Dedicated we'd discuss a term for production. We'll surface sample contract language.
08:42 - Mark Liu: Regarding the bastion, do you require a static IP from our side?
08:50 - Jonah Clark: We can use a static egress IP for the bastion, yes — simplest for firewall rules. We'll provide the IP once provisioned.
09:02 - Luis Gomez: One more on perf: can you run a test with our retrieval pipeline? We want to see end-to-end latency including vector DB calls.
09:14 - Jonah Clark: Absolutely — if you can give a small dataset and the retrieval stub or URL, we can include that in the benchmark. That will affect tail latency but it's important to measure.
09:28 - Priya Desai: We'll put together a small retrieval artifact and the sample prompts.
09:35 - Ava Martinez: Perfect. Any open security red flags? Sana?
09:42 - Sana Patel: Main ask is KMS and key rotation policy details. Also need confirmation on PII handling in logs — are the logs redacted by default?
09:53 - Jonah Clark: Logs can be redacted at the server side, we can enable PII scrubbing for certain fields and we document the scrub rules. We'll share the config and example logs.
10:06 - Mark Liu: Ok that helps. On timeline — can we aim to have peering and bastion done by next Tuesday so you can run the benchmark mid-week?
10:16 - Ava Martinez: That sounds reasonable. We'll target Jonah running bench Wednesday/Thursday once Mark confirms access.
10:25 - Priya Desai: Sounds good. Also, please include a short runbook of rollback steps in case the pilot causes any perf anomalies in staging.
10:35 - Jonah Clark: Yep we'll include rollback playbook (revert routing, disable caching changes).
10:43 - Speaker 3: (background) yeah and document the monitoring dashboards too.
10:50 - Ava Martinez: We'll share the dashboard template and invite you to the Console demo next session.
10:58 - Priya Desai: Thanks, what are the immediate deliverables after this call?
11:04 - Ava Martinez: I'll list them in the recap email but high level: runbook + security docs, perf results, RBAC matrix, and scheduling the workshop.
11:15 - Mark Liu: I'll open the ticket and add the CIDR and firewall details today.
11:20 - Sana Patel: I'll review the SOC2 and KMS notes; expect follow-up questions by Monday.
11:28 - Luis Gomez: I'll pull a small retrieval dataset and share the prompts.
11:34 - Jonah Clark: I'll run the bench once access is available, and upload to shared/benchmarks.xlsx with notes on config used.
11:44 - Ava Martinez: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items — recap and links in email.
11:52 - Priya Desai: Thanks all, talk soon.
11:55 - Meeting ended.
